claims_paid_count_pct.name: Claims paid
claims_paid_count_pct.label: Individual death claims paid by count
claims_paid_count_pct.plain: Out of every 100 individual death claims IRDAI reports for the insurer in a year, this is how many were paid.
keepInMind: These are death claims on individual life policies of every kind (term, endowment, ULIP and others), not only term insurance. IRDAI does not publish a separate term-only figure in this table.
Kyfr calculates this from two IRDAI figures: claims paid and total claims (both by number).
It counts claims, not money. A large claim and a small claim count the same.

claims_paid_amount_pct.name: Claims paid by amount
claims_paid_amount_pct.label: Individual death claims paid by amount
claims_paid_amount_pct.plain: Out of every ₹100 claimed on individual death claims in a year, this is how many rupees the insurer paid out.
keepInMind: These are death claims on individual life policies of every kind (term, endowment, ULIP and others), not only term insurance. IRDAI does not publish a separate term-only figure in this table.
Kyfr calculates this from two IRDAI figures: amount paid and total amount claimed.
It can differ from the count-based figure. IRDAI’s aggregate data doesn’t show which claim sizes were unpaid or why.

claims_repudiated_count_pct.name: Claims repudiated
claims_repudiated_count_pct.label: Individual death claims repudiated by count
claims_repudiated_count_pct.plain: Out of every 100 individual death claims IRDAI reports for the insurer in a year, this is how many the insurer repudiated (turned down).
keepInMind: These are death claims on individual life policies of every kind (term, endowment, ULIP and others), not only term insurance. IRDAI does not publish a separate term-only figure in this table.
IRDAI reports repudiated and rejected claims as separate figures. This is only the repudiated share.
The table does not say why claims were repudiated.

solvency_ratio.name: Solvency ratio
solvency_ratio.label: Solvency ratio at March year-end
solvency_ratio.plain: The solvency ratio compares the money an insurer has available to meet its obligations with the minimum IRDAI requires it to keep. A ratio of 2.0 means it held about twice the required amount.
keepInMind: IRDAI reports this as at 31 March of each year.
It describes the insurer's financial cushion. On its own it doesn't tell you how the insurer handles claims or service.

claims_rejected_count_pct.name: Claims rejected
claims_rejected_count_pct.label: Individual death claims rejected by count
claims_rejected_count_pct.plain: Out of every 100 individual death claims IRDAI reports for the insurer in a year, this is how many IRDAI records as rejected.
keepInMind: These are death claims on individual life policies of every kind (term, endowment, ULIP and others), not only term insurance. IRDAI does not publish a separate term-only figure in this table.
IRDAI reports rejected claims separately from repudiated claims.

claims_pending_end_count_pct.name: Claims pending at year-end
claims_pending_end_count_pct.label: Individual death claims pending at year-end by count
claims_pending_end_count_pct.plain: Out of every 100 individual death claims IRDAI reports for the insurer in a year, this is how many were still pending at the end of the year.
keepInMind: These are death claims on individual life policies of every kind (term, endowment, ULIP and others), not only term insurance. IRDAI does not publish a separate term-only figure in this table.
A pending claim is not a rejected claim. It had not been decided by the year-end cut-off.

persistency_61m_pct.name: 61st-month persistency
persistency_61m_pct.label: 61st-month persistency by number of policies
persistency_61m_pct.plain: Out of every 100 policies sold, this is roughly how many were still being kept up (premiums paid) in their 61st month, about five years later.
keepInMind: Based on the number of policies, as reported by IRDAI.
Many things affect persistency, including customers' own choices and circumstances. It isn't a direct measure of claims or service.

grievances_reported.name: Complaints reported
grievances_reported.label: Grievances reported during the year
grievances_reported.plain: The number of complaints (grievances) reported against the insurer during the year, as recorded by IRDAI.
keepInMind: This is a raw count. Insurers with more customers will usually have more complaints, so compare it with the insurer’s size.

grievance_resolution_pct.name: Complaints resolved
grievance_resolution_pct.label: Grievances resolved as % of grievances reported
grievance_resolution_pct.plain: Complaints the insurer resolved during the year, as a percentage of complaints reported during the year.
keepInMind: Kyfr calculates this from two IRDAI figures: grievances resolved and grievances reported.
It can go above 100% when complaints left over from the previous year are resolved during this year.
IRDAI’s table does not say whether a complaint was resolved in the customer’s favour.

incurred_claim_ratio_total_pct.name: Incurred claim ratio
incurred_claim_ratio_total_pct.label: Health incurred claim ratio (total, excl. PA & travel)
incurred_claim_ratio_total_pct.plain: For every ₹100 of net earned premium in the insurer’s health business, this is roughly how many rupees were incurred in claims. Personal accident and travel insurance are excluded.
keepInMind: Kyfr calculates this from two IRDAI figures: total net incurred claims and total net earned premium.
"Incurred" includes claims the insurer expects to pay, not only claims already paid. This is not a claim settlement ratio.
Net figures are after reinsurance. Premium earned and claims incurred can fall in different years.

solvency_ratio.name: Solvency ratio
solvency_ratio.label: Solvency ratio at March year-end (whole company)
solvency_ratio.plain: The solvency ratio compares the money an insurer has available to meet its obligations with the minimum IRDAI requires it to keep. A ratio of 2.0 means it held about twice the required amount.
keepInMind: IRDAI reports this as at 31 March of each year.
IRDAI reports this for the insurer as a whole, not just its health policies. For general insurers it can include other lines of business.
It describes the insurer's financial cushion. On its own it doesn't tell you how the insurer handles claims or service.

persons_covered_total_thousands.name: People covered
persons_covered_total_thousands.label: Persons covered under health insurance
persons_covered_total_thousands.plain: The total number of people covered by the insurer’s health insurance policies, as reported by IRDAI.
keepInMind: IRDAI reports this in thousands of persons. Kyfr converts it to lakh/crore for readability — the number is the same.
This is the total IRDAI reports, which can include people covered through group and government-sponsored schemes, not only individual and family policies.

grievances_reported.name: Complaints reported
grievances_reported.label: Complaints reported during the year (whole company)
grievances_reported.plain: The number of complaints reported against the insurer during the year, as recorded by IRDAI.
keepInMind: IRDAI reports this for the insurer as a whole, not just its health policies. For general insurers it can include other lines of business.
This is a raw count. Insurers with more customers will usually have more complaints, so compare it with the insurer’s size.

grievance_resolution_pct.name: Complaints attended
grievance_resolution_pct.label: Complaints attended as % of complaints reported (whole company)
grievance_resolution_pct.plain: Complaints the insurer attended to during the year, as a percentage of complaints reported during the year.
keepInMind: Kyfr calculates this from two IRDAI figures: complaints attended and complaints reported.
IRDAI reports this for the insurer as a whole, not just its health policies. For general insurers it can include other lines of business.
It can go above 100% when complaints left over from the previous year are attended to during this year.

family_floater_icr_pct.name: Family floater claim ratio
family_floater_icr_pct.label: Incurred claim ratio — family/floater health policies
family_floater_icr_pct.plain: The incurred claim ratio for family/floater health policies only: rupees incurred in claims for every ₹100 of net earned premium on these policies.
keepInMind: IRDAI publishes this as a ratio (e.g. 0.68). Kyfr shows it as a percentage (68%) — same number.
Smaller insurers can show big swings in segment ratios because a few large claims move the figure.

individual_non_floater_icr_pct.name: Individual policy claim ratio
individual_non_floater_icr_pct.label: Incurred claim ratio — individual (non-floater) health policies
individual_non_floater_icr_pct.plain: The incurred claim ratio for individual, non-floater health policies only: rupees incurred in claims for every ₹100 of net earned premium on these policies.
keepInMind: IRDAI publishes this as a ratio (e.g. 0.76). Kyfr shows it as a percentage (76%) — same number.
Smaller insurers can show big swings in segment ratios because a few large claims move the figure.

gross_premium_total.name: Health premium collected
gross_premium_total.label: Gross health premium
gross_premium_total.plain: The total gross premium the insurer wrote in its health business during the year — a measure of business size.
keepInMind: IRDAI reports this in ₹ lakh. Kyfr converts it to ₹ crore for readability (1 crore = 100 lakh).
Bigger isn’t automatically better or worse. It tells you scale, not quality.

net_earned_premium_total.name: Net earned premium
net_earned_premium_total.label: Net earned health premium (excl. PA & travel)
net_earned_premium_total.plain: Health premium the insurer earned during the year after reinsurance, excluding personal accident and travel. It is the bottom half of the incurred claim ratio.
keepInMind: IRDAI reports this in ₹ lakh. Kyfr converts it to ₹ crore for readability (1 crore = 100 lakh).

incurred_claims_total.name: Net claims incurred
incurred_claims_total.label: Net incurred health claims (excl. PA & travel)
incurred_claims_total.plain: Health claims the insurer incurred during the year after reinsurance, excluding personal accident and travel. It is the top half of the incurred claim ratio.
keepInMind: IRDAI reports this in ₹ lakh. Kyfr converts it to ₹ crore for readability (1 crore = 100 lakh).
